transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, thank you for seeing me. I'm here because of my eating. It's just... once I start eating those comfort foods, I tell myself, "Maria, that is enough." But my hand still goes right back to the pot. It is like I just can't make myself stop once I get started.
After eating this way, do you do anything to try to undo or compensate for it?

No, I don't do anything like that. I know some folks might try to make themselves sick or take pills or something, but I don't. I just... I mostly just sit there feeling way too full and mad at myself. But no, I don't try to undo it.
How often do you have episodes like this when you feel unable to stop eating?

Well, since my friend passed away, I'd say this has been happening most weeks. Usually... maybe once or twice a week. It mostly seems to happen in those quiet afternoons, you know, after I get home from choir or after I finish up my gardening and the house is just empty.
How long have these episodes of feeling unable to stop eating been happening at this frequency?
Well, like I said, it started after my close friend passed away. So... I'd say it's been going on for about three months now.
During these episodes, do you eat an amount of food that is clearly larger than what most people would eat in a similar situation?

Yes, I'd say so. Like I mentioned about those afternoons after choir or working out in the garden... I'll fix myself a normal plate of rice and beans, or maybe some chicken stew. But then I just keep going back to the pot for more. I don't stop until I've eaten enough for two or three whole meals. So yes, it's definitely a lot more than most folks would eat at one time.
During these episodes, do you eat even when you are not physically hungry?

Well, no, I wouldn't say that. Usually when I sit down for my meal after choir or being out in the dirt with my garden, I am actually pretty hungry to start with. I've worked up a bit of an appetite, you know? It's just... I keep going long after I should be full. But I don't usually start eating if I'm not hungry to begin with.
During these episodes, do you eat much faster than you normally would?

Well, yes, I do. I have always been a slow eater my whole life. But lately, when this happens... I eat very fast. I'll just stand right there by the kitchen counter, and I hardly even taste the food. It's like the next bite is already in my mouth before I've even finished the last one.

latest_inference.note: Rapid eating adds a third binge-eating feature; together with objectively large intake, loss of control, weekly frequency for three months, distress, and no compensatory behaviors, this supports binge-eating disorder over unspecified eating disorder.
